common_name: Miocene Dominican Amber Fossil Fruit Fly (19 Ma Hymenaea Amber Inclusion)
lineage: Cenozoic Amber Drosophilid Chronospecies (44 Ma Eocene → 0 Ma)

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.pde: u_t = D_u lap u + f(u,v); v_t = D_v lap v + g(u,v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.growth_rate: sigma(k) = largest real eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic square; no-flux is not used

parameters.note: Unique to this 19 Ma detail slot. Not the tissue-scale (98 µm) berryi parameter set and not a neighbour chronospecies' diffusivities. The nondimensional wavelength is converted to micrometres by the factor that places classical lambda_c at 1.754 µm.

empirical_claims: Classical lambda_c on the berryi metric is 1.754 µm (1.8 µm class, log10 size = -5.756).
Subcellular mode number N = tissue_lambda / detail_lambda = 98/1.754 is conserved across succini, berryi and affinis.
Detail wavelength shortens 2.040 µm → 1.754 µm → 1.718 µm from 44 Ma to 19 Ma to 0 Ma.
Modal growth rates of the semi-implicit spectral scheme track the analytical eigenvalue sigma(k).
does_not_claim: Grimaldi 1987 measured a 1.754 µm Turing wavelength on a Dominican amber inclusion.
The gallery JPEG is a scanning electron micrograph of berryi ocellar pigment.
The 100 µm scale bar printed on the gallery plate is the phenomenon size of this slot.

specimen.license_note: Project gallery fallback. Wikimedia Commons returned no Drosophila berryi file. The plate is an amber spiral labelled at 100 µm, used as the canonical specimen image for computer-vision comparison.
